title: Understanding Psychosocial Barriers to Healthcare Technology Adoption: A Review of TAM and UTAUT Frameworks
content: Background: Leveraging healthcare technology is necessary to improve human development and well-being. However, effective adoption is frequently delayed by behavioural and psycholog-ical barriers, such as perceived usefulness, trust, and organisational readiness. This systematic re-view examines the suitability of the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) and the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) frameworks in healthcare settings, focusing on understanding the behavioural, educational, and psychological factors that influence technology adoption. Methods: A total of 20 peer-reviewed articles published between 2019 and 2024 were thoroughly reviewed in this study. The psychological elements impacting technology acceptance and ways for overcoming resistance were identified by examining research that used TAM, UTAUT, or their variations in healthcare settings. Results: The review identified important or-ganisational and psychological obstacles to the use of technology in healthcare. While UTAUT provided a more comprehensive viewpoint, it needed to be modified to include context-specific factors including trust, facilitating circumstances, and educational interventions. Meanwhile, TAM's emphasis on perceived usefulness and ease of use was shown to be insufficient for dealing with complex healthcare situations. Conclusion: Both TAM and UTAUT are helpful techniques for understanding the adoption of healthcare technology when appropriately adjusted. The results highlight the importance of interventions targeting stakeholders' organisational and psychological preparation, together with the educational strategies in order to overcome opposition and enhance trust. Future research should look into integrative frameworks that incorporate behavioural, psy-chological, and instructional tactics in order to enhance the use of technology in healthcare.
